# AI Workforce OS

> AI Workforce OS is a web app that gives a business its own team of AI assistants: they draft emails, sort customer questions, prepare reports and keep routine work moving, and nothing is sent or deleted until a person approves it.

AI Workforce OS is for companies, not developers. People ask for work in plain words, typed or spoken, and AI assistants (often called AI agents) do the routine part. Answers come from the company's own documents and show the page each point came from; when the documents do not cover a question, it says so rather than guessing. Five built-in roles (Owner, Admin, Manager, Employee and Viewer) decide who can ask, who can approve and who can only look. It works with seven AI providers and a built-in offline sandbox model. Gmail, Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook and 17 other connectors connect once an owner or admin sets them up, and use practice data until then.

Key facts:

- Sending an email, posting a message or deleting something always waits for approval from a person who is allowed to approve it. Reading, drafting and routine updates, such as adding a calendar event or updating a ticket, happen on their own.
- An approval nobody decides expires after 24 hours, and nothing is sent.
- Answers come from the documents a team adds, and each point shows the page it came from. When the documents do not cover a question, it says it cannot answer rather than guessing.
- AI providers: OpenRouter, Groq, NVIDIA NIM, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Anthropic and OpenAI. The workspace sets their order, and if one is busy or unavailable the next one answers.
- Connectors (20): GitHub, Slack, Notion, Linear, HubSpot, Webhook, Jira, Confluence, Asana, Zendesk, Stripe, Zoom, Twilio, Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams and Salesforce. Each connects to a real account once an owner or admin sets it up, and uses practice data until then, so nothing real is sent.
- Ready-made example assistants: HR (hiring and onboarding), Engineering Manager (keeping projects on track), Research (market and competitor research) and Customer Support (answering customers). A new assistant can be briefed the way one would brief a new hire, and an assistant can pass work to another when a job needs more than one.
- Every workspace starts with five built-in roles composed from 47 permissions. The built-in roles are fixed, and owners and admins can create roles of their own. An employee can hand work to the AI team but cannot approve what it sends, and a viewer can look at reports but change nothing.
- Every approval decision and every finished job is recorded against the person responsible, in a tamper-evident audit chain.
- Agent traces are kept for 180 days by default, and administrators can change this.
- Provider keys and connector credentials are stored encrypted, each under its own data key and bound to its workspace.
- Routine work can run on a schedule set in plain words, such as every weekday at 9am, and can be paused at any time.
- Out of the box it runs on a built-in offline sandbox model that gives clearly labelled practice answers, so it can be tried without an AI provider key.
- The demos on the public pages run in the browser and are marked as simulated. Nothing is sent, and no account is needed.
- The platform runs as eight independent services.

## Pages

- [Home page](https://ai-workforce.bitecodes.com/): What the AI assistants do, how it works in three steps, example assistants, two demos, safety and common questions.
- [Security and technical details](https://ai-workforce.bitecodes.com/trust): For IT and security teams: the approval gate, provider failover, the tamper-evident audit chain, cited answers, the permissions of every role, what runs and the stated limits.

## Get started

- [Create your workspace](https://ai-workforce.bitecodes.com/create-workspace): The person who creates it becomes the owner and can invite everyone else.
- [Sign in](https://ai-workforce.bitecodes.com/sign-in): For people who already have a workspace account.
